sentences.text: Home sellers cut asking prices on more than 3,000 properties a day on average in Britain during September, according to figures from Rightmove shared exclusively with the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: The property website said the total was the highest of any month for 15 years and was driven, in part, by a glut of homes on the market and some sellers setting unrealistic expectations.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: The proportion of listed homes that eventually had a price cut peaked in 2023 and has remained relatively high since.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Property portals say buyers are now having to be choosy, with many working to a tight budget as mortgage rates have risen to three-year highs.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: "Once a home has been on the market for a while and then has a price reduction, some buyers start asking questions, even when there is nothing wrong with the property," said Colleen Babcock of Rightmove.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: "In a market with so much choice, first impressions matter." Rightmove data said the average price reduction was nearly 7% - the equivalent of nearly £21,000 cut from a typically valued home.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Its data showed that homes that had a price reduction typically took 119 days to find a buyer, compared with 39 days for those listed at one price.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: The proportion of listed homes that had a price reduction stood at 34% in last month, only slightly lower than the recent peak of 36% seen in September 2023.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Rival property portal Zoopla said that buyers were in the driving seat, and were being more cautious and selective about the properties they viewed.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: With mortgage rates at a three-year high , Zoopla said buyers needed to keep monthly mortgage payments affordable.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: So, while the number of homes for sale was up 5% in September compared with a year earlier, the number of sales agreed had fallen by 9% over the same period, its figures showed.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: September also tends to be the month with the most cuts to asking prices as sellers often want to complete a sale by the end of the year.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Zoopla's data showed that a quarter of newly-listed homes in September had previously been listed for sale in the last year.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Six in 10 were returning at a lower asking price.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: The problem for sellers was that these homes were taking longer to sell.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Properties that needed a price reduction were half as likely to find a buyer within the normal three-month timeframe, according to Richard Donnell, executive director of research at Rightmove. 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it Sellers who have contacted the BBC's Your Voice have pointed to the difficulties created by lots of homes on the market, and extra problems for those selling leasehold properties in England.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: One, who was selling his late father's home in south Wales, said: "The market is dead.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Lots for sale; no-one buying.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: No-one thinks it's going to get easier." Tarah Lourens, chief operating officer at Rightmove, said that "emotional" factors influenced sellers pricing a home - as they "put a value on the time and money they have invested in their home".
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: But she said that buyers simply considered everything they could buy at their budget.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Agents said that valuations now drew on huge amounts of data.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Craig Webster, of Tiger Sales and Lettings in Blackpool, said that getting an initial price correct when new to the market was crucial.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: "That's when you have the greatest opportunity to capture the attention of active buyers," he said.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Katie Griffin, from surveyors Sawdye and Harris in Devon, said that having to correct a price could ultimately lead to a seller accepting less than even a revised asking price.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: "The property may already have been online for several months and buyers can start asking why it has not sold," she said.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: But Andrew Boast, chief executive of SAM Conveyancing, said sellers might still not be losing out, if they had negotiated aggressively when buying the home and had seen it rise in value while they owned it.

sentences.text: In Scotland, the Home Report system , external requires an independent valuation of a home before it is put on the market.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: Donnell, from Zoopla, said the system gave sellers a guide to pricing.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: As a result homes sold at a faster rate than anywhere else in Britain.
sentences.article_title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day

sentences.text: His data showed that 74% of homes in Scotland listed during April, May and June sold within three months, compared with 30% in London.

sentences.text: He said that higher prices, stamp duty and some people - including landlords - not needing to sell meant that listed homes were less likely to sell in southern England.

sentences.text: The measures also seek to tackle littering, vaping and threatening behaviour to help improve journeys on all forms of public transport.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos Two Russian men secretly working for Ukraine's intelligence services have given rare accounts of operations they claim to have been involved with, that have targeted military assets and personnel inside Russia.

sentences.text: One of the men, whom we are calling Ivan, claims to have played a role from Russia in Ukrainian drone attacks on strategic bombers and munitions factories on his home soil.

sentences.article_title: Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia

sentences.text: He stresses they are never involved in the attacks themselves.

sentences.article_title: Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia

sentences.text: When Ivan's handler was pressed on whether he could be trusted, the handler replied: "I'm not sure of anyone, except myself." And both the GUR and the men are cautious about how much detail they share, making it impossible to verify the activities the men claim to have carried out.

sentences.article_title: Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia

sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: Nearby, a gaunt-looking man in a wheelchair has deep wounds in his legs, likely from xylazine use.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: He's being tended to by 40-year-old Karen Bell.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: Karen is a recovery worker with the group Liv4Lali.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: A former heroin user, she's 17 years free from hard drugs.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: She exudes kindness, and when I ask her about the drugs being used now, she says, "so many things are being mixed in right now.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: And it's affecting our bodies, whether it's the wounds, whether it's the withdrawals - and sometimes wounds can extend to the point where it's life changing." Her organisation, like Hope Dealers in Columbus, distributes test strips which check drugs for fentanyl, medetomidine, xylazine and other adulterants.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: The drugs now, says Karen, are "way more dangerous".
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: "Because before, back in my day, I stopped using heroin 17 years ago, right.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: When you bought that you knew it was heroin.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: But now, when you buy a bag, you don't know really what it is," she tells me.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: Karen, a recovery worker, tends to a gaunt-looking man in a wheelchair in an upscale part of town Dart has been sheriff of Cook County for 20 years, so I ask him how the war on drugs was progressing.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: "I don't think there's anybody involved with it who would sit there and say it's a raging success.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: And the new problem, he says, reiterating the Chicago drug dealer, is synthetics.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: "The tradition has always been that law enforcement had an even more vital role because everything that was potent was coming across the border, whether it was coming from Colombia, Mexico, China, the poppy fields of Afghanistan.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: Now, with the explosion of synthetic drugs, people can do this in their house, in their sink, in their bathtub, you name it." Victory in the war on drugs won't come from focusing just on the supply side, the sheriff adds.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: "Front and centre there's got to be huge substance abuse treatment," he says, mentioning a number of recovery programmes running in his jail.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: "You can reduce the market if you can address people's issues with substance abuse.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: And I know many people who, after long struggles, have come out on the other side in a really good way." Karen knows how difficult it is to quit.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: She was still using heroin when she got pregnant with her daughter, Abby, now 17.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: After our meeting at the metro station, I meet them both in a country park in a suburb outside Chicago.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: With typical care, Karen tells me to watch out for the poison ivy as we walk along a muddy track.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: It wasn't far from here, around 17 years ago, that she was at her lowest ebb.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: Karen says her pregnancy was an opportunity to get clean.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: She's 17 years free from hard drugs As the wind blows through a tall oak tree beside us, she says: "The day I found out I was pregnant, I was on my way to commit suicide.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: I was so fed up with trying to quit.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: I was so fed up with living in a tent in the woods, using a bucket.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: I was so fed up with losing my friends and family because I was just so ashamed." A pregnancy test changed her mind.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: She then spent time in Cook County jail for theft.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: Her parents, sensing an opportunity for her to get clean, refused to pay her bail money.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: So Karen got clean and Abby was born inside the jail.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: When I ask Abby, who wants to become a tattoo artist, whether she's ever been tempted to experiment with drugs, she says: "Nah, I've seen it mess with my family too much, with my dad, my mum, killing my aunt, my uncles.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: You know, it's not worth it to get high for like a couple of hours." She continues: "There's a lot of people are struggling, especially that our country is raising our prices, raising the prices on food and it's causing it.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: A lot of mental health now is very expensive so people can't get help, and one way they can turn to that is by drugs." Generations of Americans have endured the drugs crisis, but it is never the same crisis.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: It has shifted from heroin, to prescription opioids to fentanyl and now to a whole new range of synthetics.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: Successive administrations have fought - and lost - the war against drugs.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: The Green leader told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, it would be party policy until 2028.

sentences.article_title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: It divided the party and sparked a major backlash from MPs, Jewish campaigners, the government and the European Green movement, with the equality watchdog writing to the party for more information on it.
sentences.article_title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: The fallout from the motion overshadowed the final days of Polanski's campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, in which he came second to Labour, and threatened his leadership .
sentences.article_title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: He came under criticism for not voting on the motion which was passed by 1,022 votes to 813 - a small fraction of the party's 230,000 members - in Brighton earlier this month.
sentences.article_title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: The motion also asserted the party's backing for "a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine", a full arms embargo on Israel and a commitment to Palestinian liberation.
sentences.article_title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: Asked if he would now step in as leader to overturn it, Polanski said: "I'm not going to try to overturn it.

sentences.text: Kuenssberg asked if he would therefore change the rules as leader, but Polanski said: "I think if members have made a decision, then I respect the democratic will of our members." sentences.article_title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: "I don't think it's tenable for us to continue the next two years with this policy that's been adopted given the huge political distraction that it's been for our councillors across the country," he told the BBC News Channel.
sentences.article_title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: "One way forward could be to have a ballot of all party members to establish very clearly where does the party as a whole stand - my view is we would see a different answer." Polanski had previously said he would not have voted for the motion without two amendments.

sentences.text: Many of the records accessed were sensitive and held "intimate information" the panel said An officer who inappropriately accessed police records more than 2,000 times has been sacked for gross misconduct.

sentences.text: A West Midlands Police misconduct hearing acknowledged PC Shannon Parsons felt "isolated and disconnected" due to working part-time and returning from maternity leave, but had breached standards of professional behaviour.
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: Parsons had claimed there was a policing purpose to her searches, the panel said, and was seeking to "keep herself up to date, informed and was often in a position to support and assist other colleagues in operational matters".
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: However, chair of the panel Debra Tedds concluded the searches were carried out for the officer's "own personal benefit".
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: As a result, Parsons was dismissed without notice and barred from future work in policing.
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: The searches took part over a period of about five years, the panel heard, and many included incidents near her home address.
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: Parsons had an otherwise unblemished career in policing in the West Midlands, lasting 13 years, but was said to show no insight or remorse "as to the potential harm that has been caused by accessing the amount of information over a significant time period," according to the panel's report.
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: "Policing holds a significant amount of information about members of the public of which most of it is sensitive." She added that some of the incidents accessed by Parsons were are "of the most sensitive and hold intimate information involving some of the most serious crimes".
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: Tedds said: "I have determined that the access was for personal use.
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: Under no circumstances should anyone access or use police information for personal reasons.
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: "Accessing confidential police information without a legitimate policing purpose is an abuse of an officer's position." She concluded that amounted to a significant breach of trust, likely to cause a loss of public trust and confidence in the profession.
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: However, she added there was no evidence to suggest any of the information accessed by Parsons had been passed to a third party.
sentences.article_title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

sentences.text: "I accept that PC Parsons felt isolated and disconnected from policing and her team working part time, returning from maternity leave, and working from home as she described," she said.

sentences.text: Barnaby Webber, Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates were killed in the Nottingham attacks NHS staff accessing the medical records of the Nottingham attacks victims and possible breaches over a man killed by a tiger is a "disgrace", the health secretary has said.

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC, Yvette Cooper said she expected action to be taken against staff who had breached NHS data and privacy standards.

sentences.text: Her comments came after Nottingham University Hospitals (NUH) NHS Trust confirmed it had sacked a total of 15 members of staff and Yorkshire Ambulance Service said William Chapman's medical records may have been accessed illegitimately.
sentences.article_title: NHS data breaches a disgrace, health secretary says

sentences.text: Dr Manjeet Shehmar, NUH medical director, previously said there was "simply no excuse for accessing the records of a patient without a legitimate reason".
sentences.article_title: NHS data breaches a disgrace, health secretary says

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Cooper said "there's got to be proper respect for patients" from NHS staff.
sentences.article_title: NHS data breaches a disgrace, health secretary says

sentences.text: "Let me be really clear about this," she said.
sentences.article_title: NHS data breaches a disgrace, health secretary says

sentences.text: NUH said in May that it had sacked 11 members of staff for inappropriately accessing the victims' medical records, and had informed the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and Nottinghamshire Police of the investigation.

sentences.article_title: NHS data breaches a disgrace, health secretary says

sentences.text: Alan, 86, at a certificate ceremony on 6 October An 86-year-old man said learning to read has enabled him to read his and his wife's anniversary cards for the first time in 65 years.
sentences.article_title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'

sentences.text: Alan Hannay, from Dibden Purlieu, learned to read through the charity Read Easy, which helps adults across the country who struggle with the skill many of us take for granted.
sentences.article_title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'

sentences.text: Hannay told BBC Radio Solent: "It's changed my whole life, my confidence, changed my family life and everything around me.
sentences.article_title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'

sentences.text: "It's one of the best experiences I've ever had in my life." Hannay said he now reads every morning for about an hour and a half and goes to the class twice a week.
sentences.article_title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'

sentences.text: "I enjoy it so much now," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'

sentences.article_title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'

sentences.text: It said he asked his local library in Hythe, Southampton, about learning to read, which led him to the charity and his reading coach, Angie.
sentences.article_title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'

sentences.text: During his working life as a professional chauffeur, he relied on his memory to drive his clients around London, and at the age of 70 he attended evening classes to improve his reading.

sentences.article_title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'

sentences.article_title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'

sentences.text: "To lose a loved one in the way that the families of Ian, Grace and Barnaby have is heartbreaking enough.
sentences.article_title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

sentences.text: "I am so sorry that they have had this further compounded by the actions of these staff members." Calocane is currently serving an indefinite hospital order in a high-security facility As well as the dismissals, NUH said 15 final written warnings and two first written warnings had also been issued in total.

sentences.text: Two cases were found to have no case to answer and no action was taken.
sentences.article_title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

sentences.article_title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

sentences.article_title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

sentences.article_title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

sentences.text: The Nottingham Inquiry examined decisions made in the lead-up to fatal attacks on 13 June 2023 and the aftermath The first dismissals were made public amid a statutory public inquiry examining the lead-up to the attacks and decisions and actions taken in the aftermath.

sentences.text: The judge-led Nottingham Inquiry , external heard from 164 witnesses during 14 weeks of evidence between February and June 2026, as well as two days of closing statements from core participants in September.
sentences.article_title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

sentences.text: The findings of the inquiry, which is being led by retired senior judge Deborah Taylor KC, will be published by May.
sentences.article_title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

sentences.text: The hearings scrutinised authorities that had interactions with Calocane in the years before the attacks, laying bare failures and missed opportunities by agencies, including the NHS and police.
sentences.article_title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

sentences.text: The inquiry heard Calocane had been sectioned four times under the Mental Health Act and had a history of police interactions linked to violent incidents before the killings.
sentences.article_title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey is planning to increase taxes on the bank sector, senior banking executives have told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Healey has described banks as part of "the crown jewels" of the UK economy, but leaders in the sector have said it will be "on the menu" at the Budget in two weeks' time.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The biggest four banks collectively made about £15bn profit in the first six months of this year, and trade unions have called for them to face additional taxes.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The trade body for the banking sector, UK Finance, warned "further increases in bank taxes would weaken competitiveness, discourage investment and job creation, and work against the government's ambition to deliver growth in every postcode".
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Shares in banks including Lloyds and NatWest fell on Friday on expectations that the sector would be hit by tax hikes.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The firms were among the biggest fallers on the UK stock market, with both dropping more than 2%.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Barclays fell only slightly and HSBC actually rose as both have large international businesses and would be less affected by a hike in UK taxes.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: What is the Budget and what could be in it?
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: There are a number of ways the chancellor could extract more money from the sector.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: One option is for Healey is to reverse a reduction in the surcharge that banks pay on corporation tax, from 8% to 3%, introduced in 2023, by Conservative chancellor Jeremy Hunt.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Critics argue this would be unfair noting the cut coincided with a rise in corporation tax from 19% to 25%.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Healey could also raise the bank levy - a small percentage charged on loans.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The BBC understands that the Treasury is leaning towards changing the surcharge if they were to go ahead as it is easier to change an existing tax rather than impose a new windfall tax.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Reversing the 2023 surcharge rate would raise around £2bn.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: However, the last government was persuaded that adding 8% on top of corporation tax of 25% would leave UK banks struggling to compete with European and US rivals - so it may be that it is raised, but not all the way back to the 8% level.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Speaking to the press in Bangkok, Healey praised the role banks play in the British economy.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Sir Philip Augar, an author and former banker in the City of London, told the BBC's Today programme there was "room for a moderate increase" in taxes on the sector that could raise up to £3bn a year.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: He said lenders were enjoying "booming conditions", benefiting from higher interest rates which boost their profits.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Rising interest rates have expanded the margin between the rate at which banks lend to customers and the rate they pay savers.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Sir Philip added that when the banking sector "hits really rocky times it expects the taxpayer to bail them out - when it hits boom times, it expects some kind of special treatment".
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: He said banks cannot simultaneously be "too big to fail and too big to tax".
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Paul Nowak, general secretary of the Trades Union Congress, which represents trade unions, said Britain's four biggest banks are making a billion pounds a week, with bonuses at post-financial crash records.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: "These are bumper profits - driven by high interest rates and households' mortgage misery," he said.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: "Now it's time to make sure banks pay their fair share," he added.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: "But if the chancellor does ask the Banks to pay a fairer share of tax in the Budget, that's 100% the right call," he added.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: There is another option that has been discussed with Treasury officials.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Currently banks can use losses from the past to offset against profits - thereby reducing their tax bill in any given year.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Lloyds in particular has been a beneficiary of this policy, as large losses from the financial crisis have been used to lower tax bills ever since.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Some analysts and bank executives have pushed the idea of a moratorium on this practice for a few years, which would yield an estimated extra £1bn per year for the Treasury.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: That would provide a windfall while being "a lot more bearable", in the words of one bank executive.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: It would also spare foreign banks from an additional hit, including JP Morgan, whose chief executive Jamie Dimon has warned that the UK already has one of the highest tax burdens on banks in the world.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered by local authorities to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure the chemicals responsible for bad odours.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Europe's heatwave has boosted demand for battery storage systems As heatwaves scorched Europe this summer, workers at a US battery company noticed an uptick in demand.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: San Diego-based Unigrid sells a nine kilowatt hour battery for people's homes.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sweltering European homeowners were apparently looking for ways of storing power when it was available from the grid at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They could then run air conditioners more cheaply, off the battery, during the worst heat of the day.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We have requests coming from Spain, France, Germany, The Netherlands," says Darren Tan, co-founder and chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've shipped the first 100 units and [expect to ship] 1,000 before the end of the year." Unigrid's battery is an emerging technology – it's a sodium ion, rather than lithium ion device.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries have got energy storage experts excited because they could end up much cheaper to build and operate than lithium ion.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They're potentially less likely to catch fire and should also work in a wider range of temperatures, even down to lows of minus 40C , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Darren Tan founded Unigrid - a maker of sodium ion batteries But there's a debate over what constitutes the best, and safest, sodium ion battery design.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Plus, more than one , external US company working in this space has floundered in recent years , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: China leads the world in sodium ion battery manufacturing at present so US competitors are going to have to work hard to keep up.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The prize that awaits is the possibility of batteries made in the US with 100% US-sourced materials.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is unlike lithium ion batteries, where China dominates the materials , external supply chain as well as manufacturing.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: For Tan, China has helped his company get to market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The Unigrid battery currently uses sodium ion cells made there, rather than in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We can switch back and forth and choose what battery we want to work with," says Tan, explaining that, in future, his firm might source cells from the US – though these may come at a different cost.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: There's another consideration.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Unigrid's battery contains chromium-3 in its cathode.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In a battery, electrons flow from cathode to anode , external when charging and in the opposite direction when discharging or providing power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Ivana Hasa, at the Warwick Manufacturing Group, University of Warwick, who has no connection to Unigrid, agrees that it is possible for chromium-3 to form chromium-6 at very high states of charge, though she says this can be mitigated by how voltage is controlled within the battery.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "Safety tests reported on the cell chemistry are very promising," she says of Unigrid's tech.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Tan says concerns around toxicity of the battery's materials are "overblown" and emphasises that Unigrid's battery has passed certification and safety tests for sale in Europe and is currently undergoing such evaluations for the US market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Third-party tests have not been able to get the battery to form chromium-6, he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've tried very hard to try and produce it, we've overcharged it as much as we can...
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: We were unsuccessful in generating chromium-6." The choice of cathode material, or how the electrolyte – which separates cathode and anode – is formulated are key details influencing the performance and longevity of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some manufacturers are not using chromium for their cathode but hard carbon instead, or sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP).
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In general, confidence around sodium ion batteries' reliability has increased during the last few years, says Prof Dame Grey, meaning they are now finding their way into grid storage applications.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Last December, LFP batteries – a relatively cheap form of lithium ion battery – were trading at $81 per kilowatt hour , external (kWh) whereas Unigrid's sodium ion battery pricing is roughly $100 kWh , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some companies that spoke to the BBC suggested sodium ion might reach as low as $30 per kWh but analysts say significantly lower costs could be many years away , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries are also not as energy dense as lithium ion batteries, meaning they must be slightly bigger and heavier in order to provide the same amount of power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The technology has been improving , external on this front in recent years but, even so, you're not likely to see sodium ion cells in small, energy hungry devices such as smartphones.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Larger energy storage solutions are where most people expect sodium ion to dominate.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Emerald Battery Labs founders (left to right) Aric Stocks, Kjell Schroder, David Bell "We think sodium ion […] is going to make up 80% of the market," says David Bell, co-founder and chief executive of Seattle-based Emerald Battery Labs.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Bell declined to share details of the battery design his firm is working on, though he says Emerald too is currently relying on China-sourced sodium ion cells as they develop their initial product: 12 volt auxiliary batteries for vehicles, currently supplied to unnamed commercial fleets in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We took a look at the market and said 'Hey, no-one's trying to attack this space, let's have Emerald Battery Labs attack it'," says Bell.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The firm's next goal is to develop new anodes for US-produced sodium ion cells.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Another company, Peak Energy, based in California and Colorado, announced a partnership with General Motors (GM) in June.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The pair aim to develop a US supply chain for sodium ion batteries, in order to enable large-scale energy storage for electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Peak Energy is also, at present, relying on China-sourced cells for its first installations, but hopes to help GM launch a US-based production facility in Michigan "by the end of 2028", says Cameron Dales, president and co-founder.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "China does not have an insurmountable lead in sodium ion batteries," he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Alysm sodium ion batteries are made in the US One reason US companies feel they can compete is because of the electricity demand boom from data centres, which are contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Data centre-driven demand is also rising in other places around the world, including the UK .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is an "opportunity" says Drew Buckley, chief executive at ESS Tech, headquartered in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: He points out that sodium ion batteries could help distribute renewable energy to data centres.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And those batteries should be cheaper to run than lithium ion alternatives, since they are not expected to require as much cooling.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: ESS Tech is working with Alsym, another US firm that is planning to ship "hundreds" of megawatt hours' worth of sodium ion batteries – made in the US – by 2027.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Hasa says that it will be "challenging" for companies to establish mass production of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And she also notes that, while this type of battery is often touted as much safer than lithium ion, they do not come with zero fire risk.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: But if any firms can succeed in this space, they could enable new strategic choices, she adds – helping to avoid wastage of renewable electricity and potentially keeping energy costs low.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "I'm a strong believer in the technology," says Hasa.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The only noise is the gentle clang of the bells around the animals' necks.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This would be an idyllic scene were it not for the blackened pine and oak trees all around, the legacy of a devastating recent wildfire.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was immense, I've never seen anything like it," says Izquierdo, whose family have been farming here for 200 years.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The fire, in late July, merged with two others, burning a total of around 80,000 hectares (200,000 acres), making it the biggest blaze Spain has ever registered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: It consumed more than two-thirds of Izquierdo's land and killed 12 of his 85 cows.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another eight animals had to be put down because of their injuries.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: All the hay he had gathered to feed his cows in the winter was also burned.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "For us farmers, the summers are becoming more and more worrying, because they are getting hotter," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It rains less, the wet season ends earlier and the autumn starts much later." For farmers, such conditions are synonymous with fires.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "If you don't think about the wildfires too much, you feel okay," Izquierdo says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "But when a fire starts in a nearby village you start wondering – 'and what if we're next?'." Wildfires are one of several symptoms of climate change which in recent years have had a substantial impact on Spain's economy, as well as contributing to shocking human tragedies.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: World Weather Attribution, an international research organisation, found that the extreme conditions that drove record-breaking fires in Spain and Portugal in 2025 were 40 times more likely , external to happen due to the warming climate.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The ultimate reason for the greater frequency and intensity of these kinds of fires has to be attributed to the increase in greenhouse gases caused mainly by the generalised use of fossil fuels," said Ernesto Rodríguez Camino, president of the Spanish Meteorology Association.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Socialist Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has described the fires in dramatic terms, placing Spain in the front line of an environmental crisis.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The climate emergency kills," he said in July, during a visit to the southern province of Almería where a wildfire claimed 15 lives.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Research found that extreme heat and resulting fires in Spain were now 40 times more likely This year, around 300,000 hectares of land have been burned in Spain, according to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), approximately half the total affected in the entire European Union.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The local authorities in Castilla y León, the region most heavily affected by this year's massive fire near Madrid, are offering compensation – between €5,500 ($6,300; £4,700) and €25,000 ($29,000; £21,000) to each farmer – depending on the damage suffered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: But Izquierdo estimates that this will cover less than half of his losses.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: For decades, Spain's warm climate has been a boon for one of its other biggest industries - tourism.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Sun-drenched resorts along the Mediterranean coast, and in the Balearic and Canary Islands, have driven the country's growth as a tourist hub.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This year, close to 100 million foreigners are expected to come to Spain, making it the second most-visited country in the world, just behind France.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are signs that the heat is becoming too much for some travellers.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, this summer tested their tolerance of heat, with the country registering a record-breaking 61 days of heatwaves that continued into early September.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Toledo repeatedly saw temperatures in excess of 40C.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It's quite difficult to do the tours in the summer," says guide Diego Esteban, of the company VisiToledo.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We need to adapt, whether it is those of us who work in the tourism industry or the locals." When leading tours in the summer months, Esteban makes sure that there are frequent stops, drinking water is provided and that the itineraries include plenty of shade.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he would like to see more shade and drinking fountains available.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He says the heat has started to change the timing of the tourist season, bringing many more visitors during the cooler months of spring and autumn.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Warmer summers have also encouraged the so-called "coolcation" trend, whereby Spanish travellers seek out cooler areas to spend their holidays, typically in the north of the country.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another consequence of Spain's warming climate has been drought.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: In 2024, after three years of minimal rainfall, the north-eastern region of Catalonia temporarily introduced stringent restrictions on water use, including a 25% reduction for industry and an 80% reduction for crop farming.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Heavy rainfall since then has lifted the restrictions, but the drought had a major impact on the local economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The most dramatic and tragic natural phenomenon Spain has seen in recent years were flash floods that killed 237 people in the east of the country in October 2024, centred on the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spanish meteorological research group Climatoc-Lab described it as "a manifestation of how global warming alters the hydrological cycle".
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Valencia Chamber of Commerce estimated that the floods caused €4.5bn in direct damage.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Thousands of businesses were affected, some literally washed away by the floodwater, while others were able to resume operations after a lengthy recovery.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was a disaster, both in terms of the lives lost and the impact on businesses, on workers, employers and ordinary people," says Laura Llácer Álvarez, manager of the Fepeval federation of industrial parks in the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spain's geographical position, along with its climate and topography, make it unusually vulnerable as global temperatures increase.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Germanwatch, an independent environmental organisation, ranked Spain the world's 20th most affected country in its climate risk index for 2024, just behind Nigeria and Mali.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are those who see an upside for the economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "Climate change affects how we produce, how we invest and how we consume," says Julián Cubero, head of economics of climate change at economic think tank BBVA Research.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He points to how heat can act as a drag on economic activity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We all work worse when it's hot," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he adds, a greener economy can create new jobs with greater productivity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The key is to realise that if we don't act, growth will slow down, and if it's handled right it can become an opportunity," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Freddo the robot in action at Vsim Freddo the robot walks across the office and takes a plastic bottle offered by a staff member.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Given that a robot recently beat Usain Bolt's 100m sprint record, it's not the most startling achievement.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But the speed by which Freddo has been trained to walk, recognise the bottle and grasp it is impressive.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It took just a few minutes to develop those skills and upload them to Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: His developers say rival systems could take days to attain such skills.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: I'm at Vsim, a British start-up based in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey hope one day their software will control robots that can navigate and do useful tasks in the home and workplace.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It's a weird situation with robotics because actually the stuff that we find as humans to be incredibly difficult, like gymnastics, you can get robots to do reasonably well.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The stuff that humans are really good at, like fine dexterity, is really hard in robots," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Vsim founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey Freddo's skills were honed in a virtual environment, where a task can be performed  in a computer simulation millions of times.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Such virtual simulations are a common way to train robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Tech giant Nvidia has a system called Isaac Sim which works that way - Lu and Storey both worked on an early version of it.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: In 2022 they decided to set up Vsim, to build the their own training system environment and other tools.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "The underlying algorithms that we were using for most of these robotic simulations they hark back to the 1970s and 1980s, but those algorithms are not really brilliant fits for GPUs," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Robot training systems use virtual environments where tasks are practised Vsim is a start-up with 10 engineers working on its tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This year Nvidia has started using AI agents to help build virtual environments to train robots and validate whether the solutions from training work or not.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: They can also be trained by watching human or video demonstrations.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says their system has "reduced approximation, using accurate simulations to train models that genuinely work in reality as well as they do in simulations." Soon a second robot, to be called Nacho, will be helping develop that tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says that should speed up their development process and ensure their software can run on different machines.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And, of course, provide Freddo with some company.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained
