sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But planning a harvest is tricky.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: We guarantee less than 20% error…" Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Yasaman Ghasempour (left) is developing ripeness detection techniques Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: She and her students have come up with a millimetre wave-based ripeness detector , external that could be used by farmers – or even customers searching for perfectly ripe fruit in shops.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Her students tried it out at a local market in New Jersey.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "[Staff] there got kind of scared that we were doing something shady," laughs Ghasempour.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Such fine-grained analysis of fruit, if currently unripe, could also help inform forecasts of when it will be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Jing Zhang says new tech has to prove its worth to farmers But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Adoption is very complicated," says Jing Zhang at North Carolina State University.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works." Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries , external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The simplest systems need not be expensive.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Kevin Wang at the University of Florida has developed another crop-counting tool that can harvest imagery , external from $100 (£74) drones.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: In the future, such information could feed in to ripeness predictions.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: However, he points out that some farmers might be uneasy about sharing commercially sensitive information about their growing strategies, such as fertiliser and irrigation plans, with third parties and AI models.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Ben Palone is senior director of automation and commercialisation at Western Growers, an association that represents farmers in the western US.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He says harvest forecasts have some potential as "an optimisation tool".
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But farmers will likely continue to rely on human intelligence.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Growers like to have people in the mix to make some of those very critical decisions – especially when it comes to harvests," he says.

sentences.text: Farmer Steve Cargil is now paid $200,000 a year for hosting a solar farm on his land Steve Cargil's family has farmed the flat, dry land around Uvalde, a small city in southwest Texas, since 1953.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Cargil, 67, had always assumed that one of his three children would eventually take it over, the way he had from his father.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: But that assumption took a hit one night in 2018 after a violent hailstorm.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Cargil and his son, Ryan, had spent months nursing crops of cabbage and onions to harvest.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Then a storm rolled through and destroyed them overnight.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "I remember my son saying, 'Dad, I just don't know if I can do this.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: You do everything right, and we work so hard, and you come out one morning and it's all gone'," Cargil says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Cargil's farm was at risk of ending with him, he says, with none of his three children wanting to farm full time.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: For years, that left him wondering what would happen to the land, and to his own retirement, since farmers rarely have a pension to fall back on.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Then in 2001 Cargil signed a deal to lease 600 acres of his land, about a quarter of the total, to a company called OCI Energy which built a vast solar farm.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "Never in my wildest dreams did I think that a solar project would be on my farm," Cargil says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Looking back now, he calls it a blessing.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: The lease, which pays Cargil $200,000 (£150,000) a year, has let him keep his farm running through a punishing drought.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He has been able to concentrate his water irrigation allowance on the land he still farms, and he has stopped losing sleep over rises in the price of things such as diesel and fertiliser.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Solar farms can stretch out across the flat lands of Texas On hot afternoons, when demand for power peaks, solar is now regularly supplying around a third of the electricity used across Texas, says Mark Stover, executive director of the Texas Solar and Storage Association.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He says that the solar boom is being driven by two main things.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Firstly, it is cheap and quick to connect solar farms to Texas' power grid, which is separate to the rest of the US.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Secondly, Texas has a huge and growing appetite for electricity, driven by a burgeoning population.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2025, Texas's population increased by 15.8%, , external making it one of the fastest-growing states in the nation.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "We need a whole lot of power in Texas, and we need it quickly," Stover says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Solar has also become inexpensive.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: James Scott, vice president of project development at OCI, says the technology has had years of small manufacturing gains that brought the price down to the point where it is now the cheapest way to generate power in the state.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Reform UK is facing further questions about its vetting procedures for candidates, after undercover filming broadcast by ITV News , external .
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: In the film, gathered over the course of a year, an undercover reporter is advised by a local party chairman to delete social media posts supportive of far-right activist Tommy Robinson, before being encouraged to apply to stand to be a councillor for the party.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: It also shows a former Reform candidate claiming he failed the party's vetting process twice but was still allowed to stand to be a councillor.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Reform denies the individual failed vetting in the first place.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Reform said the party had "improved and prioritised its vetting procedures".
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Reform MP Robert Jenrick said all political parties had "bad apples".
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Today programme, he said he "didn't like what I heard in the documentary" but argued that the party had acted quickly, removing or suspending those in the undercover film.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: "I don't accept this happens any more in Reform than in any other party," he added.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: The party said: "There is no room for racism in Reform UK.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: We always respect due process of investigations and whilst these are ongoing it would not be appropriate to comment on individual cases." Reform also accused the ITV investigation of "extreme methods of deception" and using false information to obtain an undercover role in Reform's headquarters.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Jenrick said he believed the undercover reporters had wanted to find evidence of party leader Nigel Farage "acting in an inappropriate way" but had not succeeded.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Two years ago, Farage vowed to vet candidates more "rigorously", after the party dropped a series of candidates following reports they had made offensive or racist comments.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: However, the party has continued to face questions over the strength of its vetting processes.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Speaking on Thursday, before the latest filming was broadcast, Farage told BBC Look East his party vetted "to a much higher standard than other parties" but "you can't vet for future comments".
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: He meets with the chairman of a local Reform branch in Chester, Ian Frost, who describes the meeting as "the first stage" of the vetting process.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: After the reporter says he has previously posted in support of Robinson on social media, Frost advises him to delete the posts.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: "Anything where you've got, things, Tommy Robinson or anything like that, okay, I would delete the account and I'd start again," Frost adds.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Farage has said Robinson would not be allowed to join Reform.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Frost later suggests the undercover reporter could apply to stand for the party, saying: "You might become a councillor.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: You might then want to go to the MP route.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: And apply." Frost told ITV News he thought the reporter was a genuine candidate and gave him the benefit of the doubt.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: He added that it was not fair to judge people on a single conversation and he had since left Reform for unrelated reasons.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: In another part of the film, a former Reform candidate - Alex Lomas - claims he failed the party's vetting process twice, including for sharing social media posts from Robinson.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: However, Lomas says a few days after he failed for the second time he was asked to stand for the party.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: "On my second application, I got declined on the Friday, I got an email from them on the Tuesday saying you've passed vetting," he is recorded as saying.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: "I said, well, I think you better check with your paperwork, mate, because I've just failed on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Now, you're saying I've passed it, I've not changed anything.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: "And then I got a phone call a few days later.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Hi, will you stand for Reform UK?
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: I'm like, yeah okay." He stood for Reform in local elections in Oldham in May but did not win a seat on the council.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: The BBC has not been able to contact Lomas and he did not respond to requests for comment from ITV News.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Reform denies Lomas failed vetting in the first place.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: In a conversation at Reform's headquarters, the party's director of communications Ed Sumner suggests Farage is "protecting" Parry.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: In response Farage says: "It's showing a bit of sorrow." In a separate conversation several weeks earlier, where Farage was not present, Sumner is recorded saying Parry is "clearly a racist" and "needs to go".
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: After apologising to Lammy in January, Parry was allowed to remain Reform's mayoral candidate in Hampshire and the Solent until he was later suspended in March "pending investigation" , following comments about a Jewish voluntary patrol service.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: Parry told the BBC there was never an investigation and he has since left the party.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: He said: "I would urge people to go back to the original contexts and tweets to see what was said and why.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: They related to reparations and failures by the police and government.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: "They will see I always exercise my right to criticise anyone in power or the public eye, whom I judge to be acting against the interests of the British people." In the report, Reform UK MP Sarah Pochin is filmed telling the undercover reporter that the party needed "women press officers".
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: "They are so chauvinistic...
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: They just exclude you if you are a woman.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: "Nigel Farage needs to wake up and realise the buck stops with him.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: He also must urgently explain why he allegedly stood by a blatant racist instead of kicking him out of his party.
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: "Time and again Farage has had every opportunity to demonstrate leadership and get Reform's house in order and every single time he has failed." Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Reform "need to sort these issues out".
sentences.article_title: Reform faces questions over candidate vetting after undercover filming

sentences.text: She added: "Every party will have people who make mistakes and have bad apples, the difference is how you deal with it." Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has asked for Parliament's official record to be corrected after telling MPs an "individual" was "responsible for the murder" of Ann Widdecombe.
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: The prime minister had faced calls to apologise for the remarks, made during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday, with a senior Tory saying they breached the "presumption of innocence" in criminal cases.
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: A man was charged with Widdecombe's murder in July, but is yet to enter a plea for the charge and is not due to stand trial until next year.
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: A No 10 spokeswoman said a correction had been issued to Hansard, the official report of parliamentary debates, and would be "published in due course".
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: Joshua Kerry, 28, was charged in July with the murder of 78-year-old Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform spokeswoman.
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: A trial before a High Court judge is scheduled for 8 June next year, and a plea and case management hearing on 29 January.
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: Earlier this month, Kerry was also charged with preparing acts of terror including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: Speaking on Thursday, Conservative shadow Commons leader Jesse Norman accused Burnham of breaching Parliament's sub judice rule, which says MPs should not refer to pending court cases in order to avoid influencing the outcome.
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: He added that the prime minister's comments at PMQs had "breached the legal presumption of innocence".
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: He asked Commons leader Sir Alan Campbell, a government minister, to "correct the record, withdraw the remark and apologise on behalf of the prime minister".
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: In response, Sir Alan said the prime minister had "said that he misspoke, he has apologised and he has corrected the record".
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: "There is no excuse for misspeaking in the House and I am not trying to explain that away, but this prime minister is characterised by an authenticity and a passion in the way that he responds," he added.
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: "It is not unusual for prime ministers or anybody else to misspeak in the House.
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: "As long as they correct the record, which he has done, that should be put into perspective."
sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats don't tend to go for rhetorical fireworks or verbal kneecappings when grumbling about their leader.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: But that doesn't mean there hasn't been grumbling going on.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: In the last week, two members of Sir Ed Davey's frontbench have resigned because they were unhappy with him, the party's direction and how policy is decided.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: It meant the prospect of a lengthy and potentially testy meeting for Sir Ed with his MPs on Tuesday evening.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrat leader arrived smiling, flanked by several loyal MPs, but made no comment as he entered the room.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Nearly four hours later, when the meeting broke up, his deputy Daisy Cooper said: "There is overwhelming support for Ed in the parliamentary party and a real sense that we need to come together as a group." Earlier, behind closed doors, we understand Sir Ed told his MPs: "We have made changes.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: I am happy to embrace more changes.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: I want us to work as a united front." Another tacit nod to things being less than united recently.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: In recent months he has appointed a new chief of staff, Ruth Younger, and James Holt, a veteran of the party's years in coalition government, as political director.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Last week's resignations were described to the BBC by one party figure as a rather Lib Dem insurrection – dissent expressed modestly.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Neither Charlie Maynard, a former Treasury spokesman and Alison Bennett, a former care and carers spokeswoman, have been publicly explicit about the reasons for their departures and both sought to express their concerns to Sir Ed privately and discreetly.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: And, it is understood, there was no coordination between them in the timing of their resignations.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: They were departures that led to fury among some of their colleagues, irritated that it made the party look divided.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: The resignations were the most clear indicators yet of an anxiety that has been bubbling away for over a year among some Liberal Democrat MPs.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: The essence of that anxiety is a fear they are not making enough of an impression and impact for the 72 MPs they have in parliament.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: "The big frustration is the lack of cut through, being noticed.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: We are the biggest third party in the Commons in a century.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: But parliament doesn't shape things as much as it used to.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: It's about algorithms now," is how one figure put it.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: They added: "In the world of social media there is an incentive, even a financial incentive, to be divisive and extreme.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: That's a sandpit we refuse to play in." Nonetheless, the party is planning to up its social media game, but do so in line with what it sees as its authentic temperament and values.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Those around Sir Ed Davey privately acknowledge there is what they claim to be a "small group" of Lib Dem MPs who are not happy with his leadership.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: It is suggested that number isn't greater than "half a dozen" - a phrase used by several people we have spoken to.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: But the anxiety about a perceived lack of impact involves far more MPs than that.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Some previous private critics have been won over by the recent changes to Sir Ed's team and are pleased to see the government talk about issues they care about: the European Union, changing the voting system for Westminster elections and social care in England, for instance.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: They also hope the scale of their local campaigning, rather than poor national opinion poll ratings, will be more significant come the next general election.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: "But we're getting there putting in place the structures to better deal with that and keep MPs happy." "Why would we get rid of our leader when no one else is pitching to be our leader?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: We need to let Ed get on with it," said another MP.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: But they all know the underlying concern about impact – the challenge of being noticed – is real and not going away.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Little wonder perhaps that by that point, almost irrespective of someone's views on the topic, there was an appetite to talk about something else.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Burnham: Post-Brexit status quo with Europe 'not good enough for Britain' With the arrival of Andy Burnham as prime minister, that has changed, despite what he said just a few months before he arrived in Downing Street.

sentences.text: He has been happy to repeatedly lean into an argument claiming that it is time to "face up to the reality that Brexit has done more harm than good" and "the status quo is not good enough for Britain." First he made this case at the Labour Party Conference last month and now he has made it again in the House of Commons.

sentences.text: Burnham is attempting to make a two-pronged case.
sentences.article_title: Why the prime minister wants to talk about Brexit again

sentences.text: Which brings us onto the second element of his case, in the medium term.

sentences.text: In the Commons, he sought to reassure you, whatever your view on Brexit.

sentences.text: "This country in the next decade needs to know where it's going.

sentences.text: Trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays that align with their biological sex rather than their gender identity, according to new NHS England (NHSE) guidance.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: It says when this is not "clinically appropriate" then alternative arrangements should be made and the dignity and safety of all patients should be maintained.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The guidance also says staff facilities should be used by people based on their biological sex, while trusts should ensure enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, such as single-occupancy toilets, are offered.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Previous NHSE guidance suggested patients and staff could be accommodated on wards or use facilities based on their gender identity.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: That meant that a trans woman – a biological male who identifies as a woman – could have chosen to be on a women's ward, or a trans man – a biological female who identifies as a man – could have opted for a men's ward.

sentences.text: That guidance was withdrawn following the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 that under equality law the term "sex" means biological sex and "woman" refers to a biological woman.

sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: This video can not be played Same-day test helps detect hidden infections in critically ill children A pioneering same-day test has been used to detect hidden and drug-resistant infections among children in intensive care.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Respiratory samples from more than 100 critically ill young patients at London's Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH) were sent for what is known as metagenomic testing. , external It can identify bacteria, viruses and fungi from a single sample, which in many cases influences what doctors prescribe.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomics can detect infections that standard tests miss, meaning better outcomes for some critically ill patients.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: In March, 10-year-old Willow Crowther became dangerously ill with pneumonia, which triggered a seizure and multiple cardiac arrests.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Willow, from Kent, was admitted to intensive care at GOSH.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Her mum, Stacey Moore, was told she had a 50% chance of survival.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "The consultant said... we should bring our family up to say goodbye to her.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: This is how critical and in how much danger she was of passing away." The team at GOSH used metagenomics - a diagnostic test that works by sequencing all genetic material present, in contrast to conventional methods where clinicians need to decide in advance what they're looking for.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The test identified that Willow had a drug-resistant bacterial infection which needed a different antibiotic to the one she had been prescribed.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The test helped doctors identify which antibiotic would be effective in treating Willow "The fact that they had a test there available to her was paramount.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: It saved her life," said Stacey.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "It's a miracle she's here and we're extremely grateful for that," added Willow's dad, Russ.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: With the right treatment, Willow was eventually able to recover from her infection, but needed several months in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: She is one of many patients at the children's hospital to benefit from the new type of testing.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: During a study in 2024-5 metagenomic testing was used on 122 critically ill children in the paediatric intensive care unit (ICU) at GOSH.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The results have now been published in the Lancet Microbe.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomic testing analyses all genetic material in a sample and can detect thousands of different pathogens.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: By contrast, the most common method of identifying bacteria is by trying to culture them in Petri dishes, a technology that has been used since Victorian times.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Another test, PCR, can identify viruses and some bacteria, but doctors need to specify what they are trying to detect.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomics testing at GOSH was able to identify around nine in 10 bacteria and viruses and all fungi in samples.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Willow celebrated her 10th birthday in August In a quarter of cases, the results influenced prescribing decisions, including starting, stopping or changing an antibiotic.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Dr Sam Ray, consultant in paediatric intensive care medicine at GOSH and co-author of the study said traditional testing required clinicians to make an educated guess about which infection they were looking for.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "The study has helped us to spot infections we would have missed, get children on the right treatment and stop antibiotics when we know they aren't going to work.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "Removing unnecessary treatment is incredibly important for the fight against growing antimicrobial resistance." Metagenomic testing at GOSH also detected 50 organisms not identified by routine diagnostics, meaning it could play an early warning role against new infections.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Around 650 more prisoners in England and Wales are due to be released under the second tranche of the government's early release scheme.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Under the scheme, eligible prisoners are released after serving a third of their total custodial sentence rather than after 40% or 50% of the term.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: People sentenced for manslaughter, rape, serious child sex and grooming offences are excluded.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: This is not the first time a government - Conservative or Labour - has released prisoners early to make space in England and Wales' overcrowded prisons.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has looked at the reasons why ministers say this latest scheme is necessary.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The prison population in England and Wales on 12 October was 87,033, which was 97.8% of useable capacity , external .
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has previously warned the prison population will overtake capacity as soon as this November.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In the long-term the MoJ has projected that the capacity of all prisons will rise to around 99,000 by 2032 as a result of more prisons being built by this government.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: But it also projected that the prisoner population would rise to about 104,000 by 2032 if the Sentencing Act 2026 - which provides for earlier release - did not come into force.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: That is why Justice Secretary Alex Norris says there is a "prison capacity crisis" which means the government has to implement the latest early release scheme.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In total 4,500 prisoners are due to be released early by June 2027 , external .
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: About 700 offenders were released from jail early on 1 October - all of whom were serving terms of less than 19 months.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The MoJ has projected that the Sentencing Act will mean the prisoner population remains below the capacity of the prison system, rising only to around 96,000 by 2032.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The England and Wales prison population has risen significantly in recent decades with a significant uptick starting in the 1990s before reaching a record high in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The Institute for Government (IFG) think tank says this is partly the result of longer sentences.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In 2023, the average prison sentence at Crown Courts in England and Wales - which deal with more serious offences - was more than 25% longer than those handed down in 2012.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: For some crimes, the increase was greater.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Sentences for robbery in 2023 were 13 months longer on average than in 2012 - an increase of 36%.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Longer sentences mean more people being held in prison at any one time.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Former Conservative Justice Secretary David Gauke, who led an independent sentencing review for Sir Keir Starmer's government, argues this is the result of a "bidding war" by political parties since the 1990s over who can imprison people for longer.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Gauke also points out that the prison population has been rising at a time when overall crime in England and Wales has been falling, according to the official Crime Survey.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: So despite the fall in crime more people are being sent to prison - and for longer.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Another reason for upward pressure on the prison population is that more people than before are being returned to prison for breaching the conditions of their release.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: There were 51,419 licence recalls in England and Wales in the year ending March 2026, up from 40,259 in the previous year - a 28% increase.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Cassia Rowland from the IFG said most recalls are for breaches of licence conditions, such as missed appointments, rather than offenders committing further offences or posing a serious risk to the public.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: "The probation service is overwhelmed, with high caseloads and lots of vacancies putting often inexperienced staff under huge pressure," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Successive governments have pledged to increase the number of prison places - but delivery has often fallen short of those promises.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Between 2010 and 2024, when the Conservatives were in power, around 13,000 new prison places were created.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: But around 12,500 places - notably those built during the Victorian era - were closed after falling into disrepair.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: That means an estimated net total of only around 500 new prison places were added over 14 years.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In a 2024 report, the National Audit Office (NAO) cited the MOJ's "unrealistic timelines", and government bodies not working together to prioritise delivery, as reasons for the slow pace of prison building.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Work is under way on a new prison - HMP Welland - being built in Leicestershire The MOJ say around 6,500 net prison places were created between 2022 and 2025, once closures are taken into consideration.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: These include places created in three new prisons.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: However, further expansion to existing prisons has been delayed by a major supplier going into administration, according to the Prison Reform Trust.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Pia Sinha of the Prison Reform Trust told BBC Verify: "Successive governments have found it difficult to increase prison capacity because new prisons take years to plan and build, often facing planning hurdles and local opposition." The Labour government has pledged to build 14,000 new prison places by 2031.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Analysts argue that without a major change in thinking about the appropriateness of prison as punishment, or a significant long-term increase in prison building, the system in England and Wales will remain close to capacity.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: And that means governments will continue to be under pressure to implement early release schemes to avert a capacity crisis.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: It is important that teenage girls, especially, get enough iron and calcium, so Ludlam-Raine says not to become overly focused on protein at the expense of other nutrients.

sentences.text: Antonia says she wants to remain open about her health to inspire other women in business When Antonia Okonma Shittu was told she had multiple sclerosis (MS) and would be using a wheelchair within the year, she was in denial.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: The 26-year-old, who was in between acting jobs and working in a call centre, said the diagnosis was a "massive turning point" in her life.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "It does really make you think about what you want to do in life," she said.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: She looked back to what she enjoyed doing as a child - styling hair - and decided to use the shock of the diagnosis to spur her on to turn her passion into a business.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia, who grew up on a council estate in west London, bought two wigs and went door to door selling them from the boot of her car.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia with American actress Niecey Nash Almost two decades later, she is now a multi-million-pound brand owner, with current and past high-profile clients including tennis icon Serena Williams, actress Niecey Nash and model Naomi Campbell.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: She even won a Black British Business Award last week .
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia, now 44, still struggles with her health, having also received diagnoses of Graves' disease - an autoimmune condition - and heart failure, but hopes her experience running a hair empire while fitting in hospital appointments can inspire other women.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia says she saw a gap in the market when she was surrounded by "terrible" wigs while working in TV and film, including in the ITV series Bad Girls two decades ago.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "Women wanted natural-looking wigs and they just weren't available.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: They looked like helmets!" Antonia set up a Facebook page and began advertising on Gumtree.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "I had very limited resources.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: I didn't have any investors behind me.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: I come from very humble beginnings." Her experience dealing with MS has helped her success, she says.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia lost her hair when she underwent chemotherapy following a bone marrow transplant, so she knows what it is like to be "completely bald".
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: This made her relate more deeply to her customers, she explains, as she understands the loss of control some women feel when they lose their hair.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "I didn't feel like myself," she says, "but being able to put on a wig that looks something close to how your hair was, or the look you used to have, it's as though you can feel like yourself again." When she sees a woman put a wig on and her "whole face lights up", it can be "very, very rewarding".
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "When we feel good about ourselves...we're more confident, we can achieve more.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: I felt like I was changing the world, one person at a time." Antonia experienced hair loss after undergoing chemotherapy While Antonia's business, A-List Lace Hair, has grown from strength to strength, with salons in London and New York, she has been dealing with the impact of her health conditions.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: She struggles with fatigue due to her MS and uses a wheelchair, but says this has not stopped her success.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Instead, it has simply changed the way she has run her business.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "I used to feel that being a good entrepreneur was being able to do as much as I can myself," Antonia said.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "Due to my health challenges, there are days where I literally can't feel my legs, they feel like jelly, there's days where I'm completely exhausted after sleeping, I wake up completely shattered." This has forced her to "trust other people and gain strength in building a team".
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: As a woman in business, being in a wheelchair can sometimes make Antonia feel "smaller" as people often have to look down at her at industry events.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "People are often surprised when I start speaking about my business, as though they're thinking 'how have you accomplished all of this in a wheelchair?'" Antonia, who has three young children, says that being underestimated can be a good thing, and she wants to remain open about her health to inspire other women.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: She says she used to feel "weak" because of her disability, but now feels she has gained "so much strength" from sharing her experience online.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Asked what she would say to another woman who may fear her age, disability or health could get in the way of success, she says: "I would encourage them to just start." "You might not have control over your health, you might not know what tomorrow is going to bring, and you might not have all the resources.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: But start with what you do have, and let's see what could happen next." Have you been affected by the issues raised in this story?

sentences.text: The health minister accepted an independent body's recommendation of a 3.5% pay uplift but it cannot be given without a budget The Northern Ireland Executive is now seven months into the financial year without a budget.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: One of the remarkable things about this situation is the relatively muted practical impacts.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: Public sector managers have adapted to emergency budget procedures; the money still flows, services are delivered, wages are paid.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: But this week real consequences began to emerge as hospital doctors ran out of patience and announced two strikes next month .
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: The lack of a Stormont budget means the doctors cannot be given the 3.5% pay uplift which was recommended by an independent body and accepted by the health minister.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: Elsewhere in the UK doctors have had that extra 3.5% in their pay packets since April.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: Hospital doctors to strike as pay dispute continues Resident doctors in England accept pay deal and end strikes Divided executive 'speaking as one' on budget, says finance minister "I don't know long you'd like us to wait?" said Clodagh Corrigan from the doctors' union, the British Medical Association (BMA).
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: The BMA met the health minister two weeks ago, and Corrigan said they were told that there will be no pay rise before Christmas "if at all".
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: In response resident doctors will hold a 24-hour walk out on Friday 20 November while consultants and specialists will operate a much-reduced service on the following Monday.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: A nurses strike may not be far behind.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: Rita Devlin says "people have to start making decisions" to address the pressures on the health system The Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has opened a ballot , external for industrial action for the same reasons as the doctors.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: "It is despicable that, year after year, nursing staff in Northern Ireland are forced to fight for a pay award that colleagues elsewhere in the UK receive as a matter of course," said Professor Rita Devlin, executive director of the RCN in Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: "Would governments in England, Scotland or Wales allow their health service staff to go indefinitely without a pay award?
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: "So why is Northern Ireland expected to accept this?" A 3.5% pay uplift has been recommended by an independent body and accepted by the health minister Health Minister Robbie Butler has attempted to strike a conciliatory note while acknowledging there will be no movement without a budget deal.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: "I remain committed to implementing this year's pay award but unfortunately, I am currently unable to do so in the absence of a sufficient budget being agreed for my department," he said.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: There is no budget because of a consensus among the executive parties that the operation of the UK's devolution funding formula now leaves them so short that they cannot produce a workable financial plan.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: The UK government has conceded that more funding is necessary and has offered an additional £1.5bn over the next three years , with a first tranche of £525m to be paid this year.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: The Stormont parties say this is nowhere near enough.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: Discussions are ongoing between the  executive and the secretary of state On Tuesday, Finance Minister John O'Dowd laid out his position in the assembly.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: "Pressures across departments in the current financial year are around £1.6bn.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: The offer that is currently on the table is around £525m.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: "Public sector pay alone is £500m or thereabouts, and any settlement or agreement has to include money for pay uplifts for teachers, nurses and other public-sector workers." Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant has reacted with exasperation.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: "You cannot keep overspending willy-nilly and not expect consequences from that.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: It's just irresponsible," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: He held a virtual meeting with Stormont ministers on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: There was no sign of agreement.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: More discussions will be held next week.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: Bryant has suggested the absolute deadline for reaching a deal is January because at that point the money available to spend under the emergency arrangements will run out.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: A deal will need to be reached much sooner than that if strikes are to be avoided.
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: Ann Watt, the director of Pivotal think tank said this is a "very difficult situation" with "no easy solution here at all".
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: "The executive is clear that the thing they want to do most is make those public sector pay awards," she told the BBC's Sunday Politics programme .
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: "I think it's very difficult to see how that circle is going to be squared in the short time available if the pressures are three times the amount of funding available." Watt said that while a deal might be made with the UK government, "the scope to do anything this year is extremely limited given the stage we're at".
sentences.article_title: Health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay

sentences.text: She added the public sector in Northern Ireland is "much, much bigger than elsewhere in the UK" and that the funding received from Westminster has to be used on a "much bigger number of people" compared to England.
