sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Doctors also took strike action in June Hospital doctors in Northern Ireland are to strike in November over pay.

sentences.text: The British Medical Association (BMA) has warned doctors are prepared to escalate the strike action if progress is not made in addressing the pay issue, which they say has seen doctors' pay drop from upwards of 26% over the past 18 years due to below inflation pay awards.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.

sentences.text: A second head teachers' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections in England, saying it is "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale" of its members.

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The Conservatives said the plans risked "throwing away" progress made in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The vocational GCSEs will be designed to allow teenagers to progress at 16 to studying similar courses at college, including the new V-levels , which schools and colleges are teaching from autumn 2027, and T-levels .

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The final instalment of Alan Milburn's review into Neets is due to be published this autumn He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Experts warn children as young as five years old are now being groomed on social media and gaming sites Experts are urging parents to talk to their children amid warnings social media grooming is becoming "quicker" and "easier" than ever before.

sentences.text: Childline said Snapchat, TikTok and Instagram were the top platforms children named in counselling about online sexual abuse last year.

sentences.text: The companies have been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Avon and Somerset Police's child exploitation prevention officer Andri Nicolau said children as young as five can be targeted through social media, gaming and messaging platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She urged parents to encourage kids to ask for help without fear of blame or punishment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Research by the NSPCC found sexual communication offences involving children in the South West have more than doubled since the offence was introduced seven years ago, to 756 in 2024/25.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Of those, 300 were recorded by Avon and Somerset Police, 96 by Gloucestershire Constabulary and 61 by Wiltshire Police.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The charity also said Snapchat was mentioned in 324 counselling sessions about online sexual abuse between April 2025 and March 2026, a 19% increase on the previous year.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: TikTok (234) and Instagram (197) were the next most frequently mentioned platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Chris Sherwood, chief executive of the NSPCC, said: "It's deeply disturbing that hundreds of children have come to us in the past year alone, disclosing experiences of online sexual abuse linked to these popular apps and platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Aqeel used social media, including Snapchat, to arrange to meet young girls.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: He also filmed some of his offences and threatened to share intimate videos and images.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Criminals try to extort or blackmail their victims by threatening to publish the images, which have often been taken by the child themselves.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau said children spending more time online meant they were increasingly vulnerable to grooming, which is "easier" and "quicker" than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "With online gaming and social media, you have kids from five years old online, some of them have their own phones, so it can be any age," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She works with schools to inform children how to be safe online, but said they are often unaware of the risks, including not viewing people they meet online as strangers and expecting them to be "nasty" from the start.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau encouraged any child or young person who believes they are being groomed to "find someone they are comfortable with and speak to them".
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She said the police might not be the first choice, but speaking to somebody they trust is what mattered.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau urged parents to talk to their children and not take away devices or ban them from platforms, warning this could make them feel they were to blame.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Sit down with your child, tell them it's not their fault, even if they've sent indecent images of themselves," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Often, particularly if it's to do with grooming or any kind of sexual or romantic relationship, children can be really scared of being judged and embarrassed to talk," said Bradshaw.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Perpetrators are always adapting ways they can better reach young people, whether that's through gaming or social media," he said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: He said another worrying trend was young people turning to AI rather than adults for advice and support about online harms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Children are regularly being fed content that is either violent or grooming material and I think as it stands, there isn't any platform that is fully safe for them," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "I do think that the social media ban for children will help, but they need to make sure that it is enforced and social media companies are held to account." Ellen Roome has secured rights for families to get social media data from their children's accounts after they pass away.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Simmons-Read said the social media ban for under 16s , which is due to come into force in 2027, "doesn't go far enough", could be bypassed by criminals and could even discourage young people from speaking up about online grooming.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "We want tech platforms to invest more in detecting exploitation when it's happening on their platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Alongside this, tech companies must be part of the solution and meet their legal and moral obligations.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Where they fall short, the government will not hesitate to step in," the spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Kerry Smith, chief executive of the IWF, said: "We welcome the commitment to introducing nudity blocking technology on children's devices – but there really is no time to lose." Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, said it is working to "fight and prevent grooming in a range of ways".
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said: "This includes restricting contact between adults and teens they're not connected to, and using technology to find and remove known child exploitation imagery.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "We also use behavioural signals to identify accounts showing possible signs of grooming or a sexual interest in children.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Based on the strength of the signals, we either prevent them from finding and following teens or we remove their account completely." Snapchat and TikTok have all been approached by the BBC for comment.

sentences.text: The spacecraft will head to Mars's larger moon, Phobos A space mission is set to launch on Monday that will attempt to grab a piece of Mars' moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: If it is successful, this will become the first time a sample has been returned from Mars or its moons to be analysed in laboratories here on Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The spacecraft will blast off from Japan and arrive at Phobos in August 2027.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It is hoped that the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission, which is led by the Japanese Space Agency, will solve the mystery of how Mars's moons formed.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Prof Sara Russell, from the Natural History Museum, who is the MMX mission's deputy for sample analysis, said: "There hasn't yet been a successful mission to go to Phobos and bring a bit back to Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "I think this is an incredibly ambitious and fun mission," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: There are only three moons in the inner Solar System: our own Moon, and two around Mars, which are called Phobos and Deimos.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Both of these are tiny - Phobos is about 20km (12 miles) across and Deimos is about 10km (six miles) across.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: They are also irregularly shaped, looking a bit like space potatoes.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos as it arrives in the Mars neighbourhood, and then will focus on Phobos.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It plans to set down a small rover to explore the terrain, though this will be no easy feat.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Sara Russell says no one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "The moon itself doesn't have very much of its own gravity," she explained.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "But it's next to an enormous planet that's got a much higher gravity,  and that makes it much harder to get a rover onto the surface." Mars got its moons about 4.5bn years ago - but no one knows how they formed The rover will scout out a landing site so that the MMX spacecraft itself can later touch down on Phobos.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Once on the surface, it will deploy a robotic arm and two samplers to grab some moon dust.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: This material will be packed into a small capsule that will return to Earth in 2031, landing in the Woomera desert of South Australia.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The amount of material that will come back is tiny - just 10g.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "It's a very small [amount] actually," said Dr Chrysa Avdellidou, from Leicester University, who is working with the Japanese mission.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "However we can do several studies even on individual grains… You don't need to have kilos back from a surface in order to do science.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So it's worth every gram," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The spacecraft will collect 10g of moon dust from the surface of Phobos Scientists believe the sample will finally shed light on the puzzle of where Mars's moons came from.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: There are two competing ideas.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Either a space rock smashed into Mars early in its history, and Phobos and Deimos were created from the debris.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Or the moons are two wandering asteroids from the outer Solar System, which were grabbed by the Red Planet's gravity.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results," said Sara Russell.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "It should be pretty much immediately obvious.. whether it's the product of this dramatic impact or whether it's a captured asteroid.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So we'll find that out really quickly." The team is also hoping there might be an extra bonus coming back to their labs.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "One of the really exciting things is that Phobos is so close to the Mars surface that whenever there's an impact into the Mars surface, little grains might actually become implanted into Phobos itself," said Russell.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "And that means that the sample we get back may actually contain grains of Mars as well.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So it can give us really direct information about the composition and history of Mars." Martian meteorites are rare - this one is on display at the Natural History Museum Bringing material from Mars back to Earth has long been an ambition of space scientists.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The Nasa Perseverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since 2021, has been carefully collecting samples on Mars and storing them in canisters.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: But a second Nasa/ESA mission, called Mars Sample Return, that would have picked up and returned these canisters, has been effectively cancelled, after its funding was halted by the US Congress.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: China is planning its own sampling mission to Mars, set to launch in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: We do already have some fragments of the Red Planet here on Earth in the form of Martian meteorites.
sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.article_title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Martian meteorites are extremely rare, but like all space rocks that fall to our planet, they become contaminated as soon as they get here, mixing with the air, dust, soil and water.

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Speaking at Prime Minister's Questions, Burnham said he will set out decisions "shortly" Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said a decision on whether to give the go-ahead to two oil and gas fields will be made "shortly".
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: Burnham has been deliberating over plans for Rosebank, an oil field off Shetland, and gas field Jackdaw, east of Aberdeen - with a decision on the latter "imminent", according to the energy secretary.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: The controversial fields have been the subject of years of debates, legal wrangling and public consultations, with arguments from both industry bodies and environmentalists being weighed up by the UK government.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: Speaking at Prime Minister's Questions, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch urged Burnham "to stop faffing about" when it comes to the North Sea drilling.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: She said: "In July, he said he would approve the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas fields in the North Sea.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: "If he'd approved them back then, we would have British gas warming British homes this winter.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: "All of the gas from Jackdaw goes onto the British grid, so will we now stop faffing about and approve Rosebank and Jackdaw?" Jackdaw, which is about 150 miles (241.4km) east of Aberdeen, is a gas field which its operators say could be connected to the UK network within months.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: Rosebank, about 80 miles (128.7km) north-west of Shetland, is Britain's largest untapped oil field, which would also produce some gas.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: The prime minister responded: "She asked me what I'm waiting for – I've had to wait for the government process, which was struck down by the courts under the Conservative government, to be fixed because they messed it up, and we inherited that situation.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: "So I will take a pragmatic approach on oil and gas, we will set out our decisions shortly." Speaking at the Energy UK Annual Conference, Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said: "We have got all the information on Jackdaw and the department has gone through that so there is a decision that will be imminent".
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: She added a decision on the development of the Rosebank oil and gas field will take a little longer.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: The Jackdaw gas platform and drilling rig stand east of Aberdeen in the North Sea Licences for the fields were granted by the Conservative UK government in 2022 and 2023, which sparked legal challenges from environmental groups.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: The Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled last year that Rosebank and Jackdaw had been unlawfully approved because the government had failed to take into account the climate impact of burning extracted oil and gas from the sites.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: Environmentalists insist more drilling would be unconscionable, and hamper efforts to cut planet-warming carbon emissions as deadly heatwaves and extreme weather affect people across the globe.

sentences.text: They also claim starting production would not protect energy security and transitioning sooner to greener technologies would be better for supporting jobs.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: Industry bodies argue starting production at Rosebank and Jackdaw will provide jobs and improve the UK's energy security as overseas conflicts threaten supply.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: Burnham has previously left open the possibility of granting approval to Jackdaw and Rosebank.
sentences.article_title: Burnham - Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas decisions coming 'shortly'

sentences.text: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic has been drumming up support for its expected stock market listing as it seeks to reassure investors of its profit-making potential.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: Anthropic revenue surged by 45% to $16.8bn (£12.7bn) in the three months to the end of September, the BBC understands.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: In common with other AI firms, it is seeking to position itself as being able to generate huge profits despite spending billions on tech.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: It also emphasised safety at its event after warnings by current and former researchers of serious and even existential risks to humanity posed by AI.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: Anthropic's revenue has risen in successive quarters this year, from $4.7bn in the first three months to $11.6bn the following period.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: The company also told investors during the event at its headquarters in San Francisco that it had made a third quarter profit on an adjusted basis, an accounting method which ignores non-recurring costs.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: Investors reportedly left the Anthropic investor event optimistic about the company's rapid revenue growth and path to profitability.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: Alongside concerns about profit generation, there have also been fears about the safety of AI models.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: In September one of its researchers warned of a greater than 10% chance that AI could "kill all humans" within the next decade , and a former researcher said people working on the technology were "genuinely frightened" about the speed of its advancements and what it could mean for humanity .
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: A recording device (R) was wrapped in toilet paper and plugged into a TV (L) A Saudi national who worked for OpenAI appeared in court this week for allegedly planting a secret recording device behind a TV in one of the tech giant's meeting rooms.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old engineer, was arrested by the FBI and charged with using or attempting to use a device "to intercept oral communications".
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: As yet, it is not clear what he was planning to do with the recordings.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: But, here's we do know so far.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: The engineer asked AI to help him listen in to discussions about AI, according to an official complaint (the document filed in court).
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: Between 17 August and 16 September, Alfozan had reportedly asked a productivity AI assistant several questions about meeting rooms and their availability.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: Some detailed in the complaint include "how about external partners, where would they usually meet with OpenAI at" and "can you list today's meeting in this room".
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: The complaint also claimed that in September, Alfozan used a chatbot associated with his spouse to ask how to build and install a recording device and how to access it remotely.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: Alfozan had worked at the firm for around a year before he allegedly made his attempt to plant a recorder.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: The room where the device was found was regularly used to hold meetings to discuss "highly confidential technical, commercial and strategic information" as well as OpenAI's "government engagements and commercial relationships", the complaint stated.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: Alfozan had no authority to access or be involved with meetings in the room, the complaint states.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: But CCTV footage recorded him near the conference room on eight separate occasions in September.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: On 30 September, OpenAI staff discovered a "surreptitious audio recording device" behind a television - which had been wrapped in toilet paper.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: A camera was placed in the conference room and on 5 October, Alfozan was filmed entering the room and appeared to look behind the television where the device had been inserted.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: The complaint also stated that same day he allegedly left an unattended bag in a different room.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: When security personnel opened it, it was found to contain "another recording device" similar to the one discovered, as well as Alfozan's wallet and ID.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: In a post on X , external , OpenAI wrote it had used its own AI models to "understand the device and where it had come from".
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: It also said: "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data." Alfozan was captured looking behind a television where a device had been inserted Alfozan had been employed as an engineer by OpenAI since July 2025.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: The complaint said he was educated in the US and has been a legal permanent resident since 2020.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: He was arrested by the FBI on 9 October and his contract with OpenAI has been terminated.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: Alfozan's lawyer William Pernik told the BBC: "Like countless Americans, Mr Alfozan came to this country years ago as a young person with a dream.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: Like every one of us, Mr Alfozan is presumed innocent, and what has been made public is an accusation, not a finding of guilt." On Tuesday, Alfozan made his initial appearance in a federal court in California.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: A detention hearing is scheduled on 19 October to determine whether he should remain in custody while proceedings continue.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: The FBI investigation is ongoing.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.text: If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 (£190,000) fine.
sentences.article_title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer

sentences.article_title: Pony herd gathering raises money for air ambulance

sentences.article_title: Pony herd gathering raises money for air ambulance

sentences.text: This video can not be played Could using AI in your job application be ruining your chances of getting hired?
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: Would you use AI to help you write a CV or cover letter?
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: How about during an online assessment or video interview for a job?
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: We are increasingly using the technology to help us with job applications, graduates , external and recruiters say, with many employers happy for us to do so within reason.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: But when does it cross a line from being acceptable to unethical, or even cheating?
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: Tom, 22, from Maidstone graduated last year with a geography degree and says he applied for over 200 jobs before finally landing a role last month as a restaurant manager.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: He says the process was "exhausting" and "demoralising", with employers often not even getting back to him, and he wouldn't have got through it without some help from AI.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: He also thinks it's "hypocritical" for companies to ask candidates not to use AI when some are using it themselves to screen candidates .
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: "That's where it feels like a weird tightrope.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: You can't use AI too much because otherwise you're not human.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: But if you don't write like an AI, you may get skipped by the AI screening." This summer, the Institute of Student Employers (ISE) surveyed 155 of the UK's biggest graduate employers and found they were becoming "more accepting" of candidates using AI "at some stages of the recruitment process".
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: According to the trade group, the most commonly accepted use was writing cover letters or CVs, followed by completing online application questions.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: However, it also found 92% of employers had encountered or suspected AI "misconduct" in the job selection process - up from 85% last year.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: Most commonly this included using AI as a real-time assistant during online video interviews or to complete online assessments.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: On top of this, the tech is helping candidates write multiple applications at the same time - something known in the industry as "spray and pray".
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: Stephen Isherwood, joint chief executive of the ISE, says it is "driving up the competition and pressure on students" in an already competitive graduate recruitment market.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: EDF's Hollie Moody says the use of AI in job applications is a "moral dilemma" for both employers and employees Hollie Moody, head of early careers recruitment at energy giant EDF, says she doesn't blame graduates for using AI in applications given how "brutal" the jobs market is right now.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: But she does think it's becoming a problem.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: EDF opened its graduate recruitment scheme three weeks ago, but decided to close it early after receiving 12,000 applications - a 10% increase on last year.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: Moody says AI almost certainly contributed to this, adding that the tech is being used "a lot more freely" in the actual selection process.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: It only reads CVs in the later stages of the hiring process and uses skills and behaviour-based online assessments and video interviews to better assess candidates.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: But Moody says some applicants still try to bend the rules, particularly in video interviews.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: "A lot of the answers [we hear] are the same.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: Or people might pause whilst they wait for AI to come back to them with an answer.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: But he says it was only for researching roles, tidying up his CV and generating mock practise questions for video interviews.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: While he says he would never use the tech to cheat on assessments he knows people who would.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: "I know people who have applied for 100 jobs and after a while they become desperate.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: If they see everyone else is using AI, they think how can I compete?" According to the ISE, the graduate market has stabilised after a sharp fall last year but remains tough.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: Graduate roles currently attract an average of 141 applications each, it says.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: And while only 16% of employers it surveyed are using AI in the recruitment process, 29% plan to introduce it within the next year.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: Hollie Moody says EDF does not currently use AI in its recruitment process but may have to in future.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: For her, the use of AI in job applications remains a "moral dilemma" that employers and candidates will continue to grapple with.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: But she stresses it cannot replace what her firm is looking for in new recruits.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: "It's about authenticity, but also personality.
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: We want diversity of thought in the business." Have you used AI to apply for a job or are you an employer who uses AI to find the best candidate?
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire
